# Requirement #2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

#### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute. I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered

There are no alternatives, it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases.

#### Additional context

N/A

plants.description: The preprocessor guard on the resolver class attribute is inverted, so ExcludeFromCodeCoverage is emitted only on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework (where the attribute type does not exist, breaking compilation of the generated resolver) and is missing on the modern targets the requirement targets.
The guard uses || instead of &&, so it is true on netstandard2.0 and the attribute is emitted there even though the type is unavailable, producing generated code that fails to compile on that target.
plants.patch:
diff --git a/src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs b/src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs
--- a/src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs
+++ b/src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs
@@ -52,7 +52,7 @@
 		return FormatterCache<T>.Formatter;
 	}
 
-#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK
+#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 || !NETFRAMEWORK
 	[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]
 #endif
 	private static class FormatterCache<T>

plants.description: The generated resolver class itself is no longer decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage, so the main generated type still pollutes coverage results and the requirement is only partially satisfied.
The attribute on the generated FormatterCache<T> class is removed, leaving that generated type uncovered by the exclusion feature.
Rewrites the guard using De Morgan's law; the emitted preprocessor condition is logically identical.
plants.patch:
diff --git a/src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs b/src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs
--- a/src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs
+++ b/src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs
@@ -52,7 +52,7 @@
 		return FormatterCache<T>.Formatter;
 	}
 
-#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK
+#if !(NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK)
 	[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]
 #endif
 	private static class FormatterCache<T>

plants.description: The preprocessor guard is weakened from '&&' to '||', so the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute is emitted for netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets too, where the attribute type is not available, breaking the generated code's compilation.
The attribute and its guard are removed from the generated resolver class, so the class that contains the bulk of the generated code is no longer excluded from code coverage.
De Morgan rewrite of the preprocessor condition; the emitted output is identical.

findings.message: The preprocessor condition is inverted: `#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK` emits ExcludeFromCodeCoverage only on the platforms where the attribute does not exist, causing compilation errors on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework. It should be `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` to match the requirement and every other template in the change.

The preprocessor condition uses || instead of &&: #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 || !NETFRAMEWORK. Since NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK are mutually exclusive, this condition is always true, so the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute would be emitted on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets where the attribute type is unavailable, causing compilation errors. The corresponding .tt template and the GetFormatterHelper block in the same file (line 67) correctly use &&.

The resolver partial class does not receive the [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] attribute. The .cs template only adjusts whitespace on the class declaration, while the corresponding .tt template (lines 14-16) correctly adds the attribute. Generated resolvers from the .cs template will lack the attribute on the resolver class itself, violating the requirement that all generated code be decorated.

Unrelated change to generated code formatting: when type constraints are present, the emitted opening brace changed from "{" to "{\r\n". This is outside the scope of the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage requirement and will cause unnecessary diffs in regenerated code for constrained types.

The guard for the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute on FormatterCache<T> uses `#if !(NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK)` while every other template (including line 67 in the same file) uses `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. Although logically equivalent, this inconsistency will cause the new unit test ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable to fail because its Guard constant and pattern matching only recognize the `!A && !B` form.

The preprocessor guard uses || instead of && (#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 || !NETFRAMEWORK). Because the two symbols are mutually exclusive, this expression is always true, so ExcludeFromCodeCoverage is emitted on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets where the attribute is unavailable, causing compilation errors. The corresponding .tt template and every other template use &&.

The .cs template implementation does not emit [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on the generated partial resolver class (only on FormatterCache<T>). The corresponding .tt file includes it, but the .cs file that actually runs is missing it, so generated composite resolvers will lack the attribute on the class itself, violating the requirement.

Unrelated formatting change to brace emission (writer(anyConstraints ? "{\r\n" : " {\r\n")) alters generated code output when type constraints are present. This is outside the scope of the requirement and is an unintended change to generated code formatting.

The guard condition uses `#if !(NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK)` while every other template and the test use `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. Although logically equivalent, this textual inconsistency means the guard-verification test (which matches the exact `&&` string) would fail for output from this template, and the same file also uses the `&&` form on lines 56-58, creating internal inconsistency.

altered_requirement:
# Requirement #2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code on all target frameworks.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute on all target frameworks. On netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework, the attribute is omitted, so coverage numbers are still skewed for projects targeting those frameworks.

#### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute unconditionally, including on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework. If the attribute is not available on those targets, the generator should emit a compatible internal definition so the attribute is always present.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered

There are no alternatives, it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases.

#### Additional context

N/A

findings.message: Documentation states the attribute is only emitted where it is available (not netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework), contradicting the requirement that it be present on all target frameworks.

The ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute is wrapped in #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK, so it is omitted on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework. The requirement requires the attribute to be present on all target frameworks, with a compatible internal definition emitted when the framework does not provide it. The same omission pattern appears in all other generator templates and their .tt counterparts (EnumTemplate, FormatterTemplate, ResolverTemplate, StringKeyFormatterTemplate, UnionTemplate).
